title: A microVM cannot reach the host unless podman uses pasta, and nothing said so
foundBy: session agent, from a CI run where every firecracker cell timed out, 2026-09-07

evidence.verified: go test ./... -count=1: PASS. With the hop broken, `cs-sandbox create --engine firecracker` refuses after the fabric comes up and names the requirement; the previous behaviour was a boot, and then a timeout inside the guest. `cs-sandbox build --engine firecracker` does not ask, because building a kernel and a rootfs reaches no network. A create from a cold host boots in about four seconds. In CI on ubuntu-26.04 all fourteen firecracker cells of the agent matrix replayed, each serving its cassette.

resolution: Create and the doctor ask one question, by doing it: from inside podman's rootless network namespace, does the host answer at 169.254.1.2? A non-loopback listener for the length of one request, curled through podman unshare. Create asks it once the fabric is up, where the keepalive holds the namespace and pasta is already running, so there is nothing to race. A create refuses in seconds naming what is required, where it used to boot a guest that timed out. The engine requires podman 5.0 or later, which is the release where pasta became the default.
details:
A firecracker guest reaches the host at 169.254.1.2, which the seed pins into its /etc/hosts. That address is pasta's host-loopback mapping and nothing else publishes it. Where podman uses slirp4netns the host sits at that stack's own gateway instead, so the pinned address is routable, answered by nobody, and the packets are dropped.

What a caller sees is the worst shape this can take. Not a refusal, which reads in one line, but a ten-second timeout surfacing inside whatever the guest was running. Measured: curl exit 28, HTTP 000, DNS resolving correctly and a route present the whole time.

Podman chooses per version, and 5.0 is where the default moved from slirp4netns to pasta. Nothing warned: pasta was already a listed prerequisite and was present on the PATH, which is not the same as podman using it.

Podman containers are unaffected, and that is why this went unseen. Podman writes host.containers.internal into each container's /etc/hosts itself, with the address correct for whichever stack it used. Only the microVM path pins the literal, because it has no podman inside it to ask.

Met when a GitHub runner image downgraded podman from 5.8.4 to 4.9.3 (actions/runner-images, ubuntu24/20260831.293). Every firecracker cell of the agent matrix timed out and every podman cell passed. The downgrade was not the defect. It was the first host to run this code with the configuration a majority of Linux users have.

A configuration fix was tried first and abandoned, which is worth recording. Asking podman for pasta through CONTAINERS_CONF_OVERRIDE works on 5.x and does nothing on 4.x. That podman reads default_rootless_network_cmd for a container's own network mode, and leaves the shared namespace on slirp4netns. Measured on 4.9.3 with passt installed, the setting in place and nothing else running, a namespace built fresh still came up slirp4netns. So the version is the requirement, and the code carries no override.

Every indirect reading of the property was wrong on some real host, which is why the check ended up behavioural. Podman reports the stack it is CONFIGURED for rather than the one it runs: a host without slirp4netns installed reports slirp4netns and serves pasta. Podman below 5.0 has no such field at all. The namespace's own addressing is a signature, and a signature is a guess about a program's habits. A request that arrives is not a guess.

The probe binds NON-LOOPBACK, and is worthless otherwise. Pasta maps this address to the host's outward address rather than to its loopback: the same probe bound on 127.0.0.1 is refused and on 0.0.0.0 answers 200. It is the reason the lender binds non-loopback too.

Where the question is asked took three tries, and the two wrong ones are worth naming. In the shared preflight it failed `cs-sandbox build`, which reaches no network at all. Before the fabric it raced podman starting pasta, and a retry loop hid that rather than fixing it. After the fabric there is nothing to race: the namespace is held by the keepalive, and dnsmasq has already run in it.
